learningObjective: Distinguish the intent of `torch.compile` `mode` presets and identify correct behavior claims.

canonicalClaims.claim: `torch.compile`'s `mode` presets tune codegen/runtime knobs: `reduce-overhead` uses CUDA Graph capture to lower per-launch overhead; `max-autotune` enables aggressive kernel-selection/autotuning with a compile-time cost; the default mode is a middle ground. The captured graph structure is largely unchanged across modes.
conditions: CUDA tensors are used for the CUDA-relevant claims.
nonImplications: Does not imply reduce-overhead is always faster; CUDA Graphs impose their own constraints.
Does not imply max-autotune is always worth its compile time.

misconceptions.claim: Default mode emits pure Python fallback for CUDA tensors.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Default uses Triton codegen for CUDA tensors.

misconceptions.claim: Modes change which ops are captured by Dynamo.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Modes are codegen/runtime knobs; capture is by Dynamo and shape/guard rules.
CUDA Graph capture requires static shapes and stream-safe patterns.
It increases compile time by exploring more configs.

implementationFacts: reduce-overhead relies on CUDA Graph capture where safe
max-autotune expands Triton config search and enables Cutlass/GEMM template exploration in some releases
Modes tune knobs; the traced graph is unchanged
performanceScenarios: Choosing a mode depends on the workload: many-small-kernel inference benefits from reduce-overhead; long-running training may amortize max-autotune's compile cost.
